subject.title: Dashboard /compact silently wipes context once Claude CLI session is over the 1M cap

question: For Claude CLI sessions already at or over the native context cap, should OpenClaw keep deferring compaction to Claude Code, add an OpenClaw fallback/refusal path, or require a stronger native-harness contract before Dashboard `/compact` is considered fixed?
rationale: The current source and docs intentionally defer ordinary Claude CLI compaction to native ownership, while the issue asks for visible user recovery when that native path is already over cap; automation cannot safely choose that product boundary.

options.title: Fail Loud Until Native Recovery Is Proven
options.body: Make Dashboard/manual compaction refuse over-cap Claude CLI sessions with clear export/manual-prune/new-session guidance unless a valid summary is produced.

options.title: Prove And Trust Native Ownership
options.body: Keep OpenClaw's deferral model, but require live proof that Claude Code compacts/resumes without context loss under the reported over-cap scenario.

options.title: Add OpenClaw Fallback Compaction
options.body: Build a fallback summarizer/prune path for Claude CLI transcripts when native compaction cannot run, accepting the added ownership and compatibility surface.

recommendation.title: Fail Loud Until Native Recovery Is Proven
recommendation.body: Make Dashboard/manual compaction refuse over-cap Claude CLI sessions with clear export/manual-prune/new-session guidance unless a valid summary is produced.

likelyOwner.reason: They are tied to the merged native compaction ownership follow-up and are a strong routing candidate for deciding whether the current deferral contract should change.
